11. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division committed an error by not considering that Azim, Abdul, Sabu alongwith Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah executed registered deed dated 05.01.1923 infavour of Shushila Sundari Ghosh, mother of the defendant-appellants, which shows that Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah, purchaser of the land vide registered deed dated 09.06.1917, had been the owner and possessor of the land purchased and which also proves that the registered deed dated 09.06.1917 was duly executed. He also submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their claim that the debt due to ex-landlord to the extent of Tk.450/- was not paid; He again submits that the document being ancient one clearly establish right, title, interest and possession of the defendant-appellants and their predecessor. He further submits that the defendant-appellants by adducing evidence proved that the respondent-plaintiff's predecessors cultivated the land as bargadar of Shushila Sundari and that the M.R.R. Khatian was prepared duly in the name of defendants' predecessor i.e. Shushila as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the defendant-appellants relayed the land through Advocate Commissioner which is apparent from Advocate Commissioner's report as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He lastly submits that the High Court Division wrongly shifted the onus of proof of payment of debt to the ex-landlord by the vendees of kabala dated 09.06.1917 on the defendant-appellants though in view of the kabala dated 05.01.1923 the onus was squarely falls upon the respondent-plaintiffs to prove the non-payment of the dues of ex-landlord by the vendees and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. 

 "Considering the evidence adduced by the defendant-respondents it does not appear that the consideration money for the deed dated 09.06.1917 i.e. exhibit 'Ica' was paid to the ex-landlord. It appears that trial court courageously fixed the onus of such proof on the plaintiff-appellants. The rebuttal onus always lies with the other side who wants to repudiates the presumption as the C.S. record of rights hold. 

 Obviously under the aforesaid provision of law here in the present case the proof of payment of consideration money lies on the defendant-respondents who claim to pay the consideration money of the deed dated 09.06.1917.  It is to be noted that the defendant-respondents could not produce either oral or documentary evidence in sup-port of payment of the consideration money of the deed dated 09.07.1917- 

 The observation of the lower court that the defendant-respondents could establish their title & possession to the suit jute thus stands on mere conjecture & surmise having no proof of evidence." (Sic) 

 18. Section 101 of the Evidence Act lays down that whoever desire any court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependant on the existence of fact which he asserts, must prove that those facts exist and Section 103 of the Act pro-vides that the burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided in any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on the particular person. 

 20. As per the provisions of Evidence Act, the burden of proof regarding the subsequent payment of debts of the ex-landlord by the predecessor of the plaintiffs is lies upon the plaintiffs. Though PW-1 Md. Khayrat Jahan Mollah deposed in his examination-in-chief in support of his said claim but failed to adduce any corroborative evidence. The PW-2 and 3 also did not give any evidence in their respective testimony in this regard. So, such claim of plaintiffs is not proved by corroborative evidence. 

 23. From the provisions of above mentioned Section of the Evidence Act it appears that the exhibited copy of thirty years old registered document dated 05.01.1923 is being an original copy and produced before the court from proper custody as such the presumption infavour of deed no.112 dated 05.01.1923 is that the said deed is a genuine one. In such a situation the onus of proof of the allegation of the plaintiffs regarding lending money by taking signature in blank stamp and thereafter used the same to create forged document by the predecessor of the defendant nos.67 and 68 lies upon the plaintiffs. 

 27. From the discussions made above, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellants that the High Court Division committed an error of law by shifting the burden of proof upon the defendant-appellants. 

 29, But failed to adduce any corroborative evidence in support of said deposition. So, it appears that plaintiffs have failed to prove the burden which was upon them.
